run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:37:18Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy traces to 504 responses that the Envoy-based frontend-proxy itself recorded on GET /api/recommendations with response flag UT (upstream response timeout at ~15 s). The upstream chain is frontend-proxy -> frontend -> recommendation. The recommendation service's container was CPU-saturated and throttled at its 0.1-core limit from about 01:35 onward, its ListRecommendations p95 rose to 916 ms at 01:36 and its own span emission stopped from 01:41, while frontend's recommendation RPC/route spans took 15.3-19.1 s and frontend's span p90 rose from a 111-160 ms baseline to 479 ms. Chaos Mesh events name a recurring CPU-stress experiment, Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress (namespace chaos-mesh), which spawned a StressChaos object every minute from 01:34:14Z to 01:42:14Z, each reporting 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation' for ~55 s. product-catalog stayed fast, all flagd fault flags are 'off' in flagd-config, service endpoints resolve to the ready pods, and the only other cluster anomaly (fraud-detection OOMKilled/restarts at 01:17) predates the alert and is not on this path. The fault identity rests on Kubernetes events (chaos-mesh custom resources could not be read directly), so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own 'ingress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR and the error count rose from 0 at 01:38:18Z to a peak of ~44.4 per 5-minute window at 01:43:18Z, then returned to 0 at 01:49:18Z; its 'router frontend egress' client spans show 0 errors throughout, so the failures are recorded on the ingress/server side.

The failing spans are HTTP 504: sampled frontend-proxy ingress spans from 01:42:43-01:43:11Z carry error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR with durations of 15.000-15.001 s, and the paired 'router frontend egress' span carries error="true" with http.status_code=0 and the same ~15 s duration.

frontend-proxy's access log shows the exact failing request at 01:38:45.797Z: "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=LS4PSXUNUM HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout with duration field 14999 ms, i.e. Envoy's upstream response timeout, not a routing 404 or connection refusal.

In trace 3761ca9dd7eb387d96ebefddcd0680f0 the chain is visible with parent references: load-generator 'GET' (error 504, 15.16 s) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' (error 504, 15.00 s) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (error="true", 15.00 s) -> frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' (http 200, 15.34 s) -> frontend client span 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' (rpc.grpc.status_code 0, 15.34 s); the downstream product-catalog spans in the same trace completed in 29-902 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

recommendation's own span p95 for '/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' and 'get_product_list' was 3.8-145 ms from 01:22 to 01:34 and rose to 916.7 ms at 01:36:00Z; from 01:37:00Z onward no latency samples were returned for any recommendation span_name (NaN), i.e. the service stopped reporting span durations.

recommendation's span counts collapsed: '/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations', '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' and 'get_product_list' fell from ~245.6 per 5-minute window at 01:35:00Z to 142.2 at 01:37, 27.8 at 01:39 and 0 from the 01:41:00Z evaluation through 01:49, while the container kept running.

The recommendation container (pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv) was CPU-saturated and throttled: CPU usage rose from 0.0111-0.0138 cores at 01:25-01:34Z to 0.094-0.097 cores at 01:36-01:45, and its rate of throttled CFS periods rose from ~0.27-0.44 per second (01:25-01:34) to 4.15 at 01:35, ~9.4-9.7 per second through 01:45 and 4.09 at 01:46; the container's CPU limit is 0.1 core.

Chaos Mesh applied CPU stress to the recommendation workload: Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress (namespace chaos-mesh) spawned a StressChaos object every minute at 01:34:14, 01:35:14, 01:36:14, 01:37:14, 01:38:14, 01:39:14, 01:40:14, 01:41:14 and 01:42:14Z (names jn58v, gwd9j, tq59h, lwlmp, h7zr7, 6p484, vmtj8, flf8h, q55wg), and each object's Applied event reads 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation', followed ~55 s later by TimeUp and Recovered.

The recommendation pod was not restarted or redeployed: pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv is owned by ReplicaSet recommendation-5f45f75855, is Running and ready with 0 restarts and no last termination reason, and Deployment recommendation reports ready=1/available=1 on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-recommendation; its application log still shows continuous 'Receive ListRecommendations for product ids:...' lines through 01:42:22Z with no error text in the 80 newest lines (01:40:34-01:42:22Z).

frontend's own latency degraded in the same period while its error rate did not: frontend's span p90 was 111.7-159.9 ms from 01:15 to 01:29Z and 479.0 ms at 01:43:00Z, and its STATUS_CODE_ERROR series read 0 for every sampled point across 01:13-01:49Z.

recommendation's error rate was not the problem: its STATUS_CODE_ERROR series shows only isolated single-span readings of 1.11 per 5 minutes (at 01:19-01:25 and 01:36-01:39Z) against the frontend-proxy peak of ~44.4, and the recommendation-side errors observed are on '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream'; ad, cart and payment error series likewise show only isolated 1.11 readings (ad also at 01:24 and 01:26, before the chaos started) and 0 elsewhere.

product-catalog is not implicated: its span p90 stayed 1.86-1.94 ms at every sampled point from 01:13 to 01:49Z and its spans in the slow traces completed in 29-902 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

No flagd feature-flag fault was active when checked: ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo contains 12 flags (including recommendationCacheFailure, productCatalogFailure, imageSlowLoad, paymentFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, adHighCpu, adManualGc) and every one has defaultVariant "off"; this is the object's state at query time (01:50Z) and cannot prove what it was earlier.

Service wiring is intact: the recommendation Endpoints object has one ready address 100.96.4.8 pointing at pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv and the frontend Endpoints object has 100.96.2.161 pointing at pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x7pxv, so the 504s were upstream timeouts from a reachable but slow backend rather than missing endpoints.

Separate anomaly: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-dz8j9 has last termination reason OOMKilled with restartCount 3 and the only otel-demo Pod events in the window are its BackOff (01:17:06Z) and Pulled/Created/Started (01:17:21Z) events, i.e. it changed before the alert anchor of 01:37:18Z.

Hypothesis that fraud-detection's OOM kill/restarts caused the frontend-proxy error-rate alert is rejected: those events are at 01:17:06-01:17:21Z, ~20 minutes before the alert and before the chaos started, fraud-detection's error series is 0 until four 1.11 readings at 01:42-01:45Z, and the failing operation is a 504 UT upstream timeout on GET /api/recommendations, which is on the recommendation path, not the checkout/fraud-detection path.

The causal chain from the fault to the alert is inferred, not directly tagged: CPU stress saturating the 0.1-core recommendation container (throttled ~9.5 periods/s from 01:35) stretched RecommendationService/ListRecommendations beyond frontend's and Envoy's 15 s budget, so frontend's /api/recommendations took 15.3-19.1 s, frontend-proxy's router timed out (504 UT) and the ingress error spans drove the alert; the timing coincidence (chaos starts 01:34:14, throttling jumps at 01:35, p95 916 ms at 01:36, 504s from ~01:38) supports it, but no log line or tag attributes the latency to CPU stress directly.

Decide whether the recurring CPU-stress experiment for recommendation is intended: the Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress in chaos-mesh has been spawning a ~55 s CPU stress on pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv every minute, which will keep producing frontend-proxy 504s until it is paused or removed.

If recommendation CPU contention is expected, raise its 0.1-core CPU limit (or add headroom/HPA) and reconcile Envoy's 15 s upstream timeout with the recommendation SLO, since the container currently saturates 0.1 core under stress.

Check the fraud-detection pod's memory limit and OOM history separately (3 restarts, last termination OOMKilled) and verify the RequestErrorRate rule definition, which was not loaded in the queried Prometheus and could not be inspected.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name RequestErrorRate returned 0 rules (status no_data), so the alert expression, its 6.67% value and its evaluation window are unverified.

The Schedule and StressChaos specs (cpu workers/load percentage, duration, scheduler cadence) could not be read: chaos-mesh custom resources are not readable through the available Kubernetes kind list, so the fault's exact parameters rest only on cluster events.

The chaos events in chaos-mesh only extend to lastTimestamp 01:42:14Z, so whether the Schedule kept spawning experiments after that is unknown; recommendation throttling is still ~9-9.7 periods/s through the 01:45 sample and 4.09 at 01:46 (last cadvisor sample 01:46:00Z), and CPU usage drops to 0.041 cores at that point, so the tail of the incident is unknown.
CPU stress before 01:34:14Z is unknown: the chaos-mesh event view starts at 01:34:14Z even though the events window starts at 01:17Z.
flagd-config was read at 01:50Z, after the window; it shows all flags off, but change history is not integrated, so a flag value in effect earlier cannot be ruled out.
frontend application logs returned no lines for 01:33-01:44Z (status no_data), so frontend-side error text/stack traces for the slow /api/recommendations handling are unknown.

A Jaeger trace search for service recommendation in 01:38-01:44Z returned no traces (status no_data); this is consistent with its span emission stopping but is not citable as proof, and Jaeger keeps only the most recent 5000 traces.

Ingress configuration was not verified: the Ingress list query for otel-demo returned no objects (status no_data); routing is supported only indirectly by the Envoy response flag UT and by resolved Endpoints.

Which frontend-proxy routes besides /api/recommendations failed is unknown: ingress error spans carry no route label in the returned labels, and the log sample only shows the recommendations path as 504.
Error-span series were not returned for accounting, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, quote and shipping, so their error state during the window is unknown rather than zero.
Customer-facing impact and any broader blast radius beyond the load-generator's 504s are unverified.
Change history (who created the Schedule and when) is not integrated, so the origin of the CPU-stress experiment is unknown.
next_steps: Inspect the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress and its StressChaos history (spec.stressor cpu workers/load, scheduler, duration) in the chaos-mesh namespace and confirm with the owner whether it is intentional.
Pause or remove the experiment if it is not intended, then re-check frontend-proxy ingress 5xx counts and recommendation container CFS throttling.
Review the recommendation Deployment's 0.1-core CPU limit against observed load and consider raising it, and reconcile frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout with the recommendation latency SLO.
Fetch the RequestErrorRate recording/alerting rule from the alerting Prometheus and confirm its ratio computation against frontend-proxy, since it is not present in the queried rule set.
Investigate fraud-detection's OOMKilled container (memory limit vs usage) as a separate issue.
